context:
CONSULTANT'S ANSWER 20:32 CST Nov 14 (relayed to triage; it speaks for you under ruling own-consultant-speaks-for-owner): pick option 2, narrow first. Why: the only merge your rules allow onto a red main is the revert of the blamed commit (rules git-red-main-reverts and git-never-merge-failing-ci). Option 1 lets any merge typed with --base-red-ok and a reason run with no prompt, so a non-revert can land on a red main unseen: it loses accuracy and gains no speed, because the revert is just as fast under option 2. Option 3 keeps a prompt on every revert, which is waste. So a lane adds the merge-tool check that the PR reverts the breaking merge, and the no-prompt rule follows. PR #3097 waits for it. STILL OPEN: your own page pick on 01:42 CST Nov 14 reads B (option 1, the widening option) with the note "ask consultsnt for a or b and why". That is a pick plus a request for advice, so triage does not read it as handing the choice over, and the consultant's option 2 differs from your B. Say "2" (or "B") and triage closes it. Meanwhile building the revert check is safe under both options, so the coordinator is told to start it; the no-prompt rule in #3097 waits.

ANSWER to your question 20:30 CST Nov 14: You asked "ask the consultant for a or b and why". Its answer, relayed 22:59 CST Nov 13 (triage did not see it typed): option 2, narrow first, because the merge tool lets --base-red-ok push any PR onto a red main for any reason, so a no-prompt rule would let a session merge a non-fix by mistake; the tool check that the PR reverts the broken merge is built in another lane. Your pick on the page is B, option 1 (keep as written), the widening option. Triage asked the consultant again at 20:30 CST Nov 14 now that it speaks for you (ruling own-consultant-speaks-for-owner); nothing changes until it answers.

Goal: a red-main revert merges with no prompt, and no other merge onto a red main does.
Problem (risk): the rule from your 786 c pick, `Bash(merge * --confirm --head * --base-red-ok *)`, matches any merge typed with --base-red-ok and any reason. The merge tool lifts the red-main check on any non-blank reason (merge/merge.py lines 2972 to 2974), so a non-fix merge onto a red main would also pass with no prompt, and the glob also absorbs --undo-check-unknown-ok typed before it. A permission rule cannot say "revert only". The round 1 reviewer (Sonnet-class haiku) called this a safety hole (lane's report; unchecked by triage). In the cloud the same is already true: merge/cloud_allow.json allows `merge * --confirm *`. Item 786 did not say the rule was this wide.
Based on (review): round 1 FAIL at head 5e921534c, findings 1 and 3, per the lane.
Departs from: main — main asks before any local --base-red-ok merge; option 1 adds a no-prompt rule for all of them.
Meanwhile: the lane waits on this scope pick: no push, no hand-in.
home: PR #3097; ruling own-786-c-base-red-ok-settings; step allow-merge-base-red-ok; merge/merge.py lines 2972-2974; merge/cloud_allow.json
